problem:
Which of the following matrices are symmetric?

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0.5 \\ -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0.5 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}],\,R=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following matrices are symmetric?

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}],\,R=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
A square matrix $A$ is symmetric if it is equal to its transpose:

$$
A={A}^{T}
$$

Equivalently, ${a}_{ij}={a}_{ji}$ for all $i,j.$ In other words, $A$ is symmetric across its main diagonal. 

With that in mind, let's examine each matrix in turn.

- $P$ is a symmetric matrix. Indeed, $P={P}^{T}.$

- $Q$ is *not* a symmetric matrix. Since ${q}_{13}\ne {q}_{31},$ we obtain $Q\ne {Q}^{T}.$

$$
Q=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

- $R$ is *not* a symmetric matrix. Since ${r}_{12}\ne {r}_{21},$ we obtain $R\ne {R}^{T}.$

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$P$ only."
